text: # ST0001 recon: Pplr as it stands, 2026-11-02 Recon by vc, 2026-11-02, before any port work. Sources: every file under `bin/`, `lib/`, `src/`, `tests/` and `templates/`, plus the README, CHANGELOG, `usage-rules.md`, `setup.sh`, `.env.example`, the CI workflow and its last run, and the live People tree, which was counted but never read. Two peer surveys fed it: dc's boot findings and cc's survey, both 2026-11-02 07:37Z and 07:38Z in vc's inbox. Where they found something this recon missed, they are credited. ## 1. Summary - Pplr is 2,442 lines of bash (the `bin/pplr` dispatcher plus 30 `bin/pplr_*` commands), 1,681 lines of Swift (`src/pplr-contacts/main.swift`), and 1,030 lines of Python in four helpers run under `uv`. The bats suite has 99 tests in 10 files (1,229 lines) plus a 399-line helper. - **The Swift program is Pplr's engine, not just its Contacts bridge.** Besides Contacts sync it holds the people model, the About header parser, the `pplr://` marker rules, `resolve` and `links`, and the `people` listing that the Python helpers read. `lib/engine.sh` compiles it with `swiftc` on first use, into `$PPLR_ROOT/.build`. - **The Python is load-bearing:** tags (`tags.py`), contact cadence (`contact.py`), the sync plan workbook (`workbook.py`) and the email listing (`email_list.py`), plus a `python3` one-liner in `pplr_open`. hv's ruling of 2026-11-02 removes all of it. - **CI is a false green.** `tests/run_tests.sh` ends with `rm -rf "$PPLR_TEST_DATA"`, so it exits with `rm`'s status, never bats'. The last run (2026-10-13, run 38407533112) reported success with 9 failing tests on macOS and 41 on Ubuntu. - **The test suite can delete real data.** `setup()` honours an inherited `PPLR_TEST_DATA`, and both teardown and the runner `rm -rf` it (dc's finding). - **The suite is a usable parity oracle once two seams are fixed.** Every test drives `"$PPLR_BIN_DIR/pplr" ` from outside, and the 42 sync tests read Contacts from a JSON fixture (`PPLR_CONTACTS_JSON`), never the live store. But `setup()` resets `PPLR_BIN_DIR` to the checkout (dc's finding), so the suite cannot yet be pointed at another binary. - **Nothing here survives a Homebrew keg as is:** the run-time Swift build, `PPLR_ROOT`, the handler's baked path, `help --details` reading the checkout's README, and the version read from `VERSION.md`. - Other code reads Pplr's data: **Gtools** reads the People tree through `PPLR_DIR`, then `PPLR_DATA`, and the CMS that `pplr open` targets (`localhost:4360`) reads the index files. The file formats and both variable names are a contract, not an implementation detail. ## 2. How a command runs today `bin/pplr`: 1. Defaults `PPLR_DATA` to `$HOME/Dropbox/Career/People`, `PPLR_DIR` to `$PPLR_DATA`, `PPLR_ROOT` to the checkout (from its own resolved path) and `PPLR_BIN_DIR` to `$PPLR_ROOT/bin`. 2. `-v` and `--version` run `pplr_version`, which prints `VERSION.md`. No argument prints `Usage: pplr ` and exits 1. An unknown command prints `Error: Command 'x' not found.` to stdout and exits 1. 3. Exports `PPLR_CALLER_DIR=$PWD` and changes to `$PPLR_DATA`, so every command runs from the data root and resolves the caller's relative paths against `PPLR_CALLER_DIR`. 4. Rewrites any argument matching `^pplr://[a-z]/[^/]+/?$` to its folder name ("Surname, First") through `pplr_resolve`, for every command except `open`, `resolve`, `links` and `handler`, which take URLs as they are. 5. Runs `bin/pplr_` and exits with its status. Every command script then re-derives the same environment defaults itself: 25 copies of the same block. **Two ways to name a person.** `about`, `edit`, `linkedin`, `cp`, `open`, `new`, `applyicons` and `setpicfordir` take ` ` as two arguments. `tag`, `tags show`, `contact`, `refresh stamp`, `rename`, `pictures` and `sync --name/--skip` take one `"Surname, First"` (or `"L/Surname, First"`). The marker rewrite in step 4 helps only the second form. ## 4. The data contract The People tree is the user's live data: 368 people, 436 meeting folders, 366 `tags.yaml`, 262 `contact.yaml` and 7 alias files when counted on 2026-11-02. It syncs through Dropbox and is itself a git repository. **Anything the port writes into it must be byte-identical to what the legacy code writes for the same input**, or the first Rust run rewrites hundreds of files. ``` / // About/ (About).md header list, Tags line, picture line About/ (LinkedIn).webloc About/ (Contacts).inetloc About/ (Contact).md generated view of contact.yaml About/ (Picture).jpg|jpeg|png, (Profile).pdf About/tags.yaml, About/contact.yaml .index/aliases, .index/refreshed Meetings//.md | Summary.md | Notes.md Client/ .index/index.json, index.md, tags_index.json _pplr/vocabulary.yaml, cadence.yaml, templates/, icons/ _tags/index.md, .md _out/contacts-plan-.xlsx ``` Walk rules: letter folders are single upper-case letters; a person folder contains `", "`; every walk skips names starting with `_` or `.` (`index` and `json` also skip `bin`); meeting folders start with eight digits; `Icon\r` and `.DS_Store` are skipped where Finder leaves them. | File | Written by today | Format to keep | Read by | | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | | `About/ (About).md` | `new`, `tags render`, `pictures`, `sync --pull`, `rename` | verblock front matter; Note that Gtools reads `PPLR_DIR` first while pplr defaults `PPLR_DIR` from `PPLR_DATA`; they agree only while the two are equal. ## 6. The Swift engine `pplr-contacts `. Modes and what they are made of: | Mode | Pure logic | Contacts I/O | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `people` | walk the tree, aliases, marker, About and picture paths | none | | `resolve` | marker or alias to person, path inside the folder, `pplr://tag/` to `_tags/.md` | none | | `links` | rewrite `](...)` links into the tree (paths or CMS URLs) as `pplr://` URLs; follow symlinks | none | | `check` | match people to cards: pplr URL, then email, LinkedIn, phone, then name alone; field diffs | read every card, its groups and its account | | `link` | which matched cards need the URL, the group or an `.inetloc` | backup; card writes through Contacts.app; group create via the API | | `plan` | near-miss scoring (nicknames, Levenshtein, double-barrelled names, domains), confidence | read | | `applyplan` | which card gets what | backup; card create and update through Contacts.app; photos as TIFF via `sips` | | `photos`, `pull` | linked cards with no photo; what a card adds to pplr, never removing anything | read; backup; photo writes (`photos`); About writes (`pull`) | | `backup`, `dump` | none | every card to `.vcf`; every card as JSON | Facts the port must keep: - **Card writes go through AppleScript to Contacts.app.** The framework refused card updates from an unentitled tool (Cocoa error 134092), though it can create the group. `osascript` and `sips` are subprocesses, so Rust can drive them with no framework binding. - **Reads need the Contacts framework**: per-container enumeration to resolve a unified card's merged id back to a real, addressable card (iCloud first), group membership, and account kind (`home`, `other`, `none`). The `dump` mode emits exactly the JSON the test fixtures use. - **Normalisation rules** (all pure): case and diacritic folding; phones as digits with `+`, UK assumed for a leading 0, the trunk 0 dropped after nine named country codes (Italy keeps it), several numbers split on `,;·/`; Gmail addresses folded for dots and `+suffix`; LinkedIn reduced to its slug; a Markdown link read as its text. - **The marker**: `pplr:///`, lower case, accents dropped, every run of other characters one hyphen; the first form (`pplr://B/Bray,%20Martin`) is still recognised; aliases from `.index/aliases` resolve too. - **Exit codes**: 3 for no Contacts access, 4 for `resolve` finding nobody, 2 for usage, 1 for any other failure; `link` and `applyplan` stop after three failed writes. ## 7. The Python helpers - **`tags.py`**: vocabulary with seven facets in code (role, function, sector, org, relationship, place, cadence; the README says six), `also` folds and `split` maps. Its `tags.yaml` emitter sorts by facet, hand tags first. `render` inserts or replaces the generated Tags line after the first header list, rewrites `_tags/` in full, removes pages for unused tags, then writes `tags_index.json`, joined with the engine's people list. `check` exits 1 on any problem; an unknown subcommand exits 2. - **`contact.py`**: `contact.yaml` per person; roster and cadence tags from `_pplr/cadence.yaml` (`roster:` defaults, `every:` overrides, the file's own `cadence` over both); a meeting folder dated after today is "booked". `scan` takes `last` from the newest past meeting, linked by marker. `log --email N` reads the cached listing. `render` writes `(Contact).md` and removes an old `contact.md`. Seams: `PPLR_TODAY` pins the date; `PPLR_CACHE_DIR` moves the cache (default `~/Library/Caches/pplr`). - **`workbook.py`**: renders the engine's plan JSON as the four-sheet workbook, and with `--decisions` reads a reviewed workbook back into `[{person, decision, card}]`, refusing an invalid Decision or a missing Card ref. - **`email_list.py`**: numbers `mail-recent` messages, marks the person by matching `mailto:` addresses in About Email lines, and caches the listing. - **`pplr_open`** runs `python3 -c 'urllib.parse.quote(...)'` to percent-encode a CMS path. ## 8. Installed today - `~/.local/bin/pplr` is a symlink to `~/Devel/prj/Pplr/bin/pplr`: the user runs the checkout. - `PPLR_DATA` is unset in the login shell, so the default applies. - Toolchain on rhadamanth: Rust 1.99.1 from Homebrew (no rustup, so a `rust-toolchain.toml` would be ignored), Swift 6.4.2, bats 1.14, `jq`, `uv`, `fileicon`, `claude`; no `mail-recent` (dc, cc). - The estate runs `cargo` and `bats` in single-slot heavy lanes shared with the Devbin and Utilz sessions, granted through `intent estate slots`. ## 13. Precedent for the port and the release Summarised from Cldr, Ccusage and devbin 0.1.19; ST0002's design carries the release detail. - **House style (Cldr is the newest and canonical; Ccusage ships Python, so it is not a model for tooling):** one crate at the repo root; edition 2024; `rustfmt.toml` with `tab_spaces = 2`; `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, `unwrap_used` and `expect_used` denied; a 9-line `main.rs` calling `cli::run`; `lib.rs` as the module list; a hand-rolled CLI with a `HELP` constant and small `take_value` and `take_flag` helpers (no clap, anyhow or thiserror); `Box` errors that name the file or setting; "pure core, thin shell", with writes through a temp file; each dependency commented with why; unit tests in each module returning `Result`; one integration file, `tests/cli.rs`, with a `Sandbox` that redirects HOME, XDG and PATH (devbin's `check autotests` refuses a second `tests/*.rs`); no hand-written counts in tests. - **`forbid` cannot be relaxed** by an inner `#[allow]`, so framework bindings such as `objc2-contacts` would need the crate lint lowered or a second crate. Ccusage reaches macOS through the safe `security-framework` crate; nothing here uses objc2. - **TCC**: Cldr's Full Disk Access grant lands on the terminal that runs it. A CLI's Contacts grant does the same today ("the app running pplr, eg iTerm or Terminal"), which is why the engine needs no signing. - **Release**: Cldr renders a source-build formula into `matthewsinclair/homebrew-cldr`; Ccusage ships Developer ID signed tarballs (for Keychain access) and builds from source on Linux. devbin 0.1.19's release core and `formula: mode: source` cover what Pplr needs without either project's bespoke tools.
